## 0. Preflight

Start from a clean, up-to-date `main` in this worktree, on a fresh branch:

```sh
git status                                   # must be clean; never git stash
git fetch origin main && git checkout -b release/prep-$(date +%Y-%m-%d) origin/main
git submodule update --init -- submodules/distilled
pnpm install
bun --version                                # must be 1.3.13 — 1.4 fails every file at collection
# if not: mkdir -p /tmp/bun1313 && (cd /tmp/bun1313 && npm i --no-save bun@1.3.13)
#         export PATH=/tmp/bun1313/node_modules/.bin:$PATH   (prefix every pnpm test with this)
node -v                                      # alchemy CLI needs >= 24.11.1 and pnpm wants 24.x — node 25
# makes pnpm print a [WARN] that breaks scripts/ensure-built.ts. If not 24.11+:
#   mkdir -p /tmp/node24 && (cd /tmp/node24 && npm i --no-save node@24)
#   export PATH=/tmp/node24/node_modules/.bin:$PATH
# Put these PATH exports + `set -a; source .env; set +a` in /tmp/release/env.sh and
# source it before every command — env doesn't persist between shell calls.
set -a; source .env; set +a                  # Cloudflare creds (pnpm download:env if missing)
aws sso login                                # AWS live + nuke ride the SSO session
mkdir -p /tmp/release
pnpm exec tsrs -b                             # REQUIRED before live runs: emits distilled lib/
```

Runtime bundles (Lambda, Fly, Hetzner, Neon Functions) resolve distilled
packages through their `lib/` build output, not `src/`. A fresh worktree has
no `lib/` for most providers, so every deployed runtime would crash at boot
with `Cannot find package '@distilled.cloud/…'`.

Never set or unset `CI` for tests (a profile-store migration can wipe
`~/.alchemy`). If an AWS run fails in ~100ms during setup, the SSO session has
expired — re-run `aws sso login`.

## 1. Clean slate

```sh
pnpm nuke --yes --profile testing            # scripts/nuke.sh requires --profile; no --yes hangs
pnpm clear:state --profile testing --yes --no-input   # prompts without --yes, fails in a non-TTY
pnpm nuke --dry-run --profile testing > /tmp/release/census-0.txt   # baseline; should be residue only
```

Never run nuke while any suite is running. Holdouts that survive two nuke
passes are stuck deletes — put that service on the worklist; its delete path is
the bug. Documented-undeletable residue (excluded in `scripts/nuke.sh`, e.g.
`AWS.BackupSearch.SearchJob`, zone singletons) is not a finding.

## 2. Build the plan and dry-run it

Tests carry tags (`unit`, `live`, `local`, `provider:<cloud>`,
`provider:<cloud>:<service>`). `--tags` takes expressions with `&&`, `||`, `!`,
parentheses and `*`; `--plan` takes a JSON array of sequential phases, where a
nested array runs branches in parallel and **the first matching branch wins**.
Tags listed under `optInTags` only run when named explicitly (wildcards and
negations don't count) — never name one without asking; they gate paid add-ons
and entitlements.

Default plan (drop providers outside the scope):

```json
[
  { "tags": ["unit && !live"] },
  [
    { "tags": ["live && provider:aws"],        "concurrency": 32 },
    { "tags": ["live && provider:cloudflare"], "concurrency": 16 },
    { "tags": ["live && provider:gcp"],        "concurrency": 16 },
    { "tags": ["live && !provider:aws && !provider:cloudflare && !provider:gcp"], "concurrency": 8 }
  ],
  { "tags": ["local"], "concurrency": 8 },
  { "tags": [] }
]
```

- Phase 1 runs the unit tests first: a broken unit layer makes every live
  failure noise, so stop and fix it before spending cloud time.
- The final `[]` branch is the catch-all for untagged tests. Everything it
  picks up is a tagging gap — add the missing tags in the release PR.
- Never use `"unbounded"` and never exceed 32 per branch. Saturation shows up
  as hundreds of 0ms `beforeAll` TimeoutErrors; real failures fail slow.

Write the plan to `/tmp/release/plan.json` and preview it:

```sh
pnpm test --profile testing --plan "$(cat /tmp/release/plan.json)" --dry-run
```

For reference, on 2026-10-09 the default plan selected 11,614 tests in 2,880
files (unit 3,089 · aws 3,361 · cloudflare 1,577 · gcp 2,085 · other live
811 · local 592 · untagged 99 in 19 files). Collection takes ~10s. Check
the branch counts against expectations. A branch with 0 tests is an
invocation bug (bad tag, quoting), not a pass. Show the user the preview
before the real run.

## 3. Run it

A full round can outlast a 2-hour background-task limit, so detach it and
watch the output file with a monitor that filters to failed results
(`grep -E "\] ✗ |failed to run|^Tests:"` — a bare `✗` also matches the
`[n/N ✓ ✗]` progress counter on every line):

```sh
nohup pnpm test --profile testing --plan "$(cat /tmp/release/plan.json)" \
  > /tmp/release/round-1.out 2>&1 & disown
```

Keep running notes in `/tmp/release/STATE.md` (round, blockers, worklist,
residue) so the loop survives context compaction.

Note the `Full log: .alchemy/log/test/…` path at the end. Failures print
inline with their error as soon as they happen, so start triage at the first
failure rather than waiting for the run to finish. If nothing finishes for 10s
the runner lists running tests — a test stuck far past its timeout is a hang
to fix, not something to wait out. Check the "queued for an exclusive lock"
entries in that list before calling it a hang: those tests haven't started.

Test time is the release's biggest cost, so one slow or exclusive test must
never hold up the rest of a run. If it does, fix the runner or narrow the
lock; don't lower concurrency and don't wait it out. Tests that only contend
for a shared cloud resource take a label (`{ exclusive: "aws:ses-account" }`)
instead of `exclusive: true`, which only process-global state needs. On
2026-10-31 a writer-preferring `exclusive: true` gate froze the AWS suite
twice behind a 25-minute ElastiCache test.

## 4. Triage

Group failures by their most specific `provider:<cloud>:<service>` tag (the
service is the unit of ownership). Classify each:

| Bucket | Signal | Fix lands in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Provider bug | wrong reconcile/diff/delete, leak, crash | `packages/alchemy/src/…` (alchemy PR) |
| Untyped error | `Unknown*Error`, out-of-union status error, wrong schema | distilled patch (distilled PR) |
| Emulator bug | only fails under floci | `submodules/floci` (floci PR) |
| Test bug | non-deterministic or hard-coded name, unbounded wait, missing propagation retry | the test (alchemy PR) |
| Platform/entitlement | plan-gated, slow async provisioning, beta API | skipIf-gate on the typed tag + exact error, keep an ungated probe |
| Flake | passes alone, fails under load | re-run alone and on main first |

Root-cause priority is **provider bug > distilled patch > test fix**, and a
longer timeout comes last, only for work that is slow by nature (image
builds, cold starts). Never paper over a provider leak or untyped error in a
test. A failure that only shows up in some runs is usually two runs touching
the same cloud object — a shared name or stage, a missing lock label, or a
retry that leaks — not a flake; see the isolation rules in the harden skill.
Skip a test only for a permanent account blocker (quota, entitlement), with
`test.provider.skip` and a comment quoting the exact error. For suspected flakes,
build a verdict table: `Failure | Re-run alone | On main | Verdict`. A failure
that also fails on main is still in scope for the release — it just isn't a
regression.

## 5. Census

After the run finishes (and never while one is running):

```sh
pnpm nuke --dry-run --profile testing > /tmp/release/census-1.txt
diff /tmp/release/census-0.txt /tmp/release/census-1.txt
```

Every new resource is a leak, and a green service can still leak. **Leave the
leaked resources live** as evidence for the fix agents. The worklist is
failing services ∪ leaking services.

## 6. Fix fleet

Launch one agent per service on the worklist, in parallel. In T3 Code each
fixer is a detached top-level thread from `t3_thread_launch` with
`workspaceStrategy: { type: "existing_worktree", worktreePath: <this worktree> }`,
never a `delegate_task` subagent thread. Collect each result with
`t3_thread_wait` + `t3_thread_read`. Run ~12 at once (
account-singleton services like CloudTrail, Config, SecurityHub, GuardDuty,
ControlTower and IdentityCenter run as one sequential chain). Agents work in
this worktree and **commit but don't push**; they touch only their service's
files, plus single minimal insertions in shared files. The prompt is a
contract — include every item:

1. The service it owns, its directory, and its tag (e.g. `provider:aws:ec2`).
2. Its exact failures (error text + test names) and its leak inventory from the
   census diff.
3. Assess-first: partial work may exist from an interrupted run; finish it
   rather than rewriting.
4. Reading list: AGENTS.md Reconciler doctrine + Typed Error Doctrine + speed
   doctrine, the resource source, the test, and the distilled service +
   existing patches.
5. Root-cause priority (provider > distilled > test) and the rule that it
   never hides a leak in the test.
6. **No `tsc`, no `pnpm build`, no `pnpm nuke`** — the coordinator owns these.
7. Speed doctrine: every run is
   `pnpm test --tags '<its tag>' --profile testing`; per-test
   timeouts ≤ 90–120s; every retry bounded (`times ≤ 8–10`, < 60s total);
   three-iteration budget, then gate and report.
8. Distilled patches for its service only, regenerated in place:
   - Cloudflare: `cd submodules/distilled/packages/cloudflare && bun scripts/generate.ts --resource <svc> && pnpm exec oxfmt src/services/<svc>.ts`
   - AWS: `cd submodules/distilled/packages/aws && bun scripts/generate.ts --sdk <svc>`
   Tests resolve distilled from `src/`, so there's nothing to rebuild or wait for.
9. Test rules: start and end with `stack.destroy()`, out-of-band verification
   through distilled, no mocks. Names: let the resource generate the physical
   name. Only a test about explicitly provided names passes one, and it is
   derived from `stack.stage` so it is isolated to the user running the test.
   Never `Date.now()`, UUIDs or random values in a name: every run is
   deterministic and leaves no orphans. A resource the API can never delete
   keeps one shared constant name that every run adopts. Fix any hard-coded
   name you find in the suites you touch.
10. Done means: its **full** tag passes, and distilled list/describe calls show
    zero orphans from its service.
11. Structured result: `{ service, tag, testsPassed, testCommand, rootCause,
    files, patches (with reasons), skippedTests (with exact errors), leaksFixed,
    notes }`.

While agents run, watch for stalls: a transcript that hasn't been written for
~5 minutes with no child test process is stalled — `t3_thread_interrupt` it
and re-dispatch with a new `t3_thread_launch`.

When results come in, review each diff yourself before accepting it. Reject
any that catch a catch-all error, widen a cast, add `Effect.orDie` to a
lifecycle op, mock a response, or skip a test without a typed reason.

## 7. Gate

```sh
pnpm exec tsrs -b                             # coordinator only, once per round
pnpm docs:check-jsdoc                        # if any props/attrs changed
```

Fix cross-cutting fallout yourself (`Providers.ts` nested `Layer.mergeAll`
groups, barrel conflicts). Commit the round — one commit per service fix,
conventional-commit scoped (`fix(aws/ec2): …`) — and **push immediately**.

## 8. Loop

**Converge with targeted runs, then confirm with full ones.** Live tests are
slow, so after the first full plan every fixing run is targeted:

1. **Track passes cumulatively.** Every run (yours and the agents') writes
   `PASS <file> > <title>` lines to `packages/alchemy/.alchemy/log/test/*.log`.
   Rebuild the passed set from all logs, not just the last round:
   ```sh
   cat packages/alchemy/.alchemy/log/test/*.log | grep -E "^PASS " \
     | sed -E 's/^PASS //; s/ \([0-9.]+m?s\).*$//' | sort -u > /tmp/release/passed.txt
   ```
2. **Compute the residual:** tests with a `FAIL` line and no `PASS` line, plus
   tests that never finished (a killed or stalled round) — find those by
   diffing the runner's "still running" lists against the result lines.
3. **Fix agents get each failing area passing individually** (their own
   suites, `-t` for single tests in long sequential files).
4. **One residual run** of only what's still unpassed — file paths, narrowed
   with `-t` where a file is long and sequential (e.g. `Fly/BlueGreen.test.ts`
   has ~180 tests at ~100s each; never run it unfiltered).
5. **Confirm stability per provider** with the harden skill's loop: full
   runs of each provider's suite, a census after each, until two consecutive
   runs are green and clean. One green run proves little — retry leaks, lagging
   listings and shared names only show up across runs.
6. **Finish with nuke + clear:state + census.** The goal is consecutive green
   runs and a census that shows `Nothing to delete`.

If a census leftover reappears after nuke, its `list` or `delete` is the bug
(e.g. `list` returning archived or Cloudflare-managed objects), not the test.

Report each round to the user, briefly:

```md
### Round N: 1834 passed · 12 failed · 3 leaking services

| Service | Tag | Failure | Bucket | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| EC2 | provider:aws:ec2 | InternetGateway delete timeout | provider bug | fixed, 63/63 |
| R2 | provider:cloudflare:r2 | UnknownCloudflareError 10058 | distilled | patched, 30/30 |

Next: round N+1 (full plan).
```

## 9. PRs

At most three, one per repo. Open them as soon as there is a first fix, and
push every later fix promptly.

**distilled** (only if there are patches) — work in a standalone clone, never
a `git worktree add` from inside `submodules/distilled` (its `core.worktree`
belongs to another checkout):

```sh
git clone --reference submodules/distilled https://github.com/alchemy-run/distilled /tmp/release/distilled
cd /tmp/release/distilled && git checkout -b fix/release-prep-$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
# copy the patches + regenerated services from submodules/distilled, commit per service
```

Title: `fix: typed errors and schema fixes from release prep`. The body lists
each patch with the error it types, e.g. `R2 putBucketLifecycle: code 10058 →
LifecycleRuleInvalid`.

**floci** (only if emulator fixes are needed) — floci is skipped by default
(`git submodule update --init --checkout -- submodules/floci`); use the same
standalone-clone pattern against `https://github.com/alchemy-run/floci`. If alchemy needs the new emulator image, it needs a release
tag.

**alchemy** — branch `release/prep-<date>`, title
`fix: release hardening (<date>)`. It contains the provider, test, gating and
tagging fixes, plus submodule bumps pointing at the distilled/floci PR heads.
The merge order is distilled → floci → alchemy. After each upstream PR merges,
repoint the submodule at its **`main` merge commit** (never a side branch),
rerun the affected tags, and push.

Descriptions follow AGENTS.md's PR conventions: one plain sentence, then
user-facing snippets or a per-service table of what was fixed. No `#`/`##`
headings and no test plan. Write the body to a file and pass `--body-file`.
Link every PR to this thread with the T3 `link_pull_request` tool when it's
available. Leave PRs as drafts until the gate passes, then `gh pr ready`.

## 10. Final report

End with the merge ask:

```md
### Release prep converged after N rounds. I recommend merging, in this order:

1. distilled — <what it types>
   https://github.com/alchemy-run/distilled/pull/X
2. alchemy — <K> service fixes, <G> gated tests, <T> tagging fixes
   https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/pull/Y

| Phase | Tests | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unit | 856 | ✅ |
| live provider:aws | 1662 | ✅ 1650 · 12 skipped (gated) |
| … | | |

Gated (needs entitlement / platform): <test → exact error>.
Fails on main too (pre-existing, now fixed): <list>.
Census: clean except <documented residue>.
```

Say plainly what was **not** run (out-of-scope providers, opt-in tags). Don't
report CI status in place of the test results.

## Pitfalls seen in practice

- **Commit with the pinned env sourced.** The pre-commit hook runs pnpm; with
  the wrong bun/node or a stray temp workspace dir under `examples/` (left by
  a killed test) it re-installs and rewrites `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Never commit
  the lockfile or Prisma `generated/contract.*` churn.
- **Distilled regeneration can `pnpm install` inside `submodules/distilled`**,
  creating a nested `node_modules` with a second `effect` copy ("Unable to get
  redacted value" everywhere). Move `submodules/distilled/node_modules` aside
  and check `packages/*/node_modules/effect` links point at the root store.
- **Other sessions share the account.** Another worktree's live resources
  show up in your census; check `ps -eo etime,command | grep alchemy-test`
  before deleting a leftover you can't trace to your own run. A linked
  worktree defaults to its own test stage (`test_$USER_<worktree>`), so two
  worktrees don't collide; suites that set their own stage must prefix it
  with `Test.defaultStage()`.
- **Provider `console.log` doesn't reach the run log.** Debug with
  `Effect.logInfo`, and probe API behavior with a throwaway test file rather
  than guessing.
- **Account blockers are not code.** Billing (GCP), token permission groups
  (e.g. Cloudflare K2) and retired services (AWS FinSpace) get reported to the
  user with the exact error; never enable billing or edit shared tokens.

# Write the release blog

The post covers every PR merged to `origin/main` since the most recent
`chore(release)` commit, and announces the next version. The house rules for
release posts live in AGENTS.md ("Blog / Release Notes Conventions"); this
skill is the procedure. Read the last two posts in
`website/src/content/docs/blog/` (`*-beta-*.md`) before writing. They set the
voice, length and structure to match.

## 1. Collect every PR

```sh
.agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/collect-prs.sh /tmp/release-blog-<next>
```

It prints the release commit (`chore(release): 2.0.0-beta.N`, so the post is
for `beta.N+1`) and writes one JSON per PR, a `digest.txt` with every PR's
title, author and full body (oldest first), and `authors.txt` with every
non-maintainer author's display name.

## 2. Read every description in full

Read all of `digest.txt`, in chunks, start to finish. It holds whole bodies,
on purpose: a PR's later sections ("### Changes", a second snippet, a
"Removed" list) are where secondary features and renames hide, and a post
planned from excerpts folds them into a clause or drops them. Don't sample,
and don't skim by title: a `chore` or `test` title can carry a user-facing
fix, and a `feat` body often holds the best snippet for the post.

Tag each PR as you go:

- **breaking**: `!` in the title, or `Breaking`/`[!CAUTION]` in the body. Note
  the migration diff the PR gives. Unmarked PRs break things too: look for
  "renamed", "removed", "replaces", "is gone", "now requires", "`X` is now
  `Y`" and "was `X`" in every body. Confirm each one shipped in the last
  release (`git grep <old name> <release-sha> -- packages/`) before listing
  it; a rename of something added in this same release isn't breaking.
- **headline**: a dependency upgrade users must make (Effect, a framework
  major), a new provider or package, a new capability with a user-facing API,
  or a major bug fix (data loss, wrong resource deleted or taken over,
  deploys that hang or fail, large perf or bundle wins).
- **also**: smaller features and fixes users would notice.
- **skip**: internal only. CI, skills, lint and repo tooling, test-only PRs
  that fix no shipped behavior, distilled bumps without a user-visible change,
  docs restyles, and fix-ups of earlier PRs in the same release.

Group related PRs into one item: a stack of PRs for one feature is one
section, and a family of fixes (drift, ownership, local dev) is one bullet.

## 3. Plan before writing

Write the plan out first: the title, the breaking-change list, the ordered
headline sections with the PRs each one cites, and the also-list groups.

- **Title**: `2.0.0-beta.N - <three short items>`. It renders in the blog
  sidebar, so it must fit on one line.
- **Order the headlines** by how much they change a user's day: required
  upgrades (Effect) first, then new providers and packages, then the biggest
  new capabilities, then major fixes. There is no cap on the number of
  sections; a large release gets 25–30. Its size is set by what shipped.
- **A new user-facing API gets a snippet**, in its own section or in a
  section about its area (a "New AWS resources and options" section collects
  smaller ones). Never shrink one into a clause of an unrelated section: a
  reader skimming headings must find it. A PR that adds several APIs (a store
  that gains `accountId`, `workerName` and `domain` plus a new bootstrap
  command) is usually its own section.
- **Everything else** goes into `## Also in this release`, grouped by area
  (Cloudflare features, Cloudflare fixes, Local dev fixes, AWS features, AWS
  fixes, GCP, Domain, Auth, …), each group one bullet with its PR links.

## 4. Write it

File: `website/src/content/docs/blog/YYYY-MM-DD-beta-NN.md`, dated the
release day (ask if it isn't today). Frontmatter `title`, `date`,
`category: release` and a one-sentence `excerpt`.

- Open with two short paragraphs naming the headline features in bold.
- `:::caution` with **Breaking changes** at the top. Each item says what to
  do, with a `diff` snippet when code changes, and links its section below.
- One `##` per headline. One or two sentences, then a snippet of the
  user-facing API. Show DX, not implementation: what you write, what you get,
  the before/after error or output. Take snippets from the PR bodies, trim
  them, and check the names against the source (`grep` the export) since PRs
  get renamed in review.
- End a section with `Docs: [Page](/path)` links when a page covers it.
- Cite PRs inline as `([#NNN](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/pull/NNN))`.
- Credit external contributors by display name from `authors.txt`, linked to
  their GitHub profile: `Thanks [Name](https://github.com/login)!`. Use the
  login when there's no display name. PRs a maintainer opened on someone's
  behalf say so in the body ("carries #N by", "ported from", "supersedes");
  credit that person.
- End with `## Where to go next`: doc links, then
  `[CHANGELOG](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v200-betaNN)`
  and `[Compare v2.0.0-beta.N → v2.0.0-beta.N+1](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/compare/v2.0.0-beta.N...v2.0.0-beta.N+1)`.

Format every snippet the way oxfmt would at an 80-column print width (the
blog's code column), and move trailing comments that overflow onto their own
line. oxfmt reads a top-level `yield*` as multiplication, so format such
snippets by hand or inside a temporary `function* () {}` wrapper.

Style: plain, direct sentences; no marketing adjectives; no "X just
happened" lists explaining a snippet. Every ```diff block needs a context line
at column 0 (a comment, an import, the outer call), and `+`/`-` lines are the
marker followed by the line's real indentation. Inline code that contains a
backtick uses double-backtick delimiters.

## 5. Check it

```sh
python3 -I .agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/check-post.py website/src/content/docs/blog/<post>.md /tmp/release-blog-<next>
```

It checks that every docs link and anchor resolves and that every diff block
passes the website build's odd-indent check. Fix every problem it reports.
It also lists every `feat`, `fix`, `perf` or `!` PR the post doesn't cite.
Each one must be a deliberate skip (a fix-up of another PR in this release,
test or CI only); cite the rest.

Then hand the post to the user with the headline plan (sections and the PRs
behind each), the breaking-change list, and anything you weren't sure about:
a PR whose user impact was unclear, a section you cut, or the date. Don't
commit, push or open a PR unless asked.

## 6. Tweets (when asked)

One tweet per major category, in the post's order: Effect, each headline
Domain feature, each headline provider feature, state, CLI, and one for the
bug fixes. Each tweet is one sentence plus a screenshot of its section.

**The sentence** states the user-facing change and, when the post has one,
its number: "a million accounts in 8 minutes", "plans are 270× faster".
Plain words, no hype, no hashtags, no emoji. Take every claim from the post,
not from memory.

**The screenshot** is the section's heading plus its code, diagram or table,
with the prose between them hidden. Run the docs dev server
(`cd website && bunx astro dev --ignore-lock`), list each heading's blocks,
then write a `shots.json` that picks them:

```sh
PW=$(ls -d node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@*/node_modules | tail -1)
URL=http://localhost:4321/blog/<post-slug>/
NODE_PATH=$PW bun .agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/screenshot-sections.mjs $URL --list
NODE_PATH=$PW bun .agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/screenshot-sections.mjs $URL /tmp/tweets-<next> shots.json
```

```json
{
  "01-effect-41": [["effect-41", "h"], ["effect-41", 1], ["effect-41", 3]],
  "02-domain-rollout": [
    ["deploys-roll-out-every-change-to-a-model", "h"],
    ["how-it-scales", 1],
    ["how-it-scales", 5]
  ]
}
```

Each entry is `[heading id, "h" | n]`, where `n` is the block index `--list`
prints under that heading; blocks can come from different headings. Images
are dark mode at 2× resolution, and animated figures render their last frame.
Pick the block that shows the change best: the diagram over the prose, the
failure output over the test code, the before/after table over the setup.
Open every image and check that no code line is cut off and no neighbouring
text shows.

# Write the release blog

The post covers every PR merged to `origin/main` since the most recent
`chore(release)` commit, and announces the next version. The house rules for
release posts live in AGENTS.md ("Blog / Release Notes Conventions"); this
skill is the procedure. Read the last two posts in
`website/src/content/docs/blog/` (`*-beta-*.md`) before writing. They set the
voice, length and structure to match.

## 1. Collect every PR

```sh
.agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/collect-prs.sh /tmp/release-blog-<next>
```

It prints the release commit (`chore(release): 2.0.0-beta.N`, so the post is
for `beta.N+1`) and writes one JSON per PR, a `digest.txt` with every PR's
title, author and full body (oldest first), and `authors.txt` with every
non-maintainer author's display name.

## 2. Read every description in full

Read all of `digest.txt`, in chunks, start to finish. It holds whole bodies,
on purpose: a PR's later sections ("### Changes", a second snippet, a
"Removed" list) are where secondary features and renames hide, and a post
planned from excerpts folds them into a clause or drops them. Don't sample,
and don't skim by title: a `chore` or `test` title can carry a user-facing
fix, and a `feat` body often holds the best snippet for the post.

Tag each PR as you go:

- **breaking**: `!` in the title, or `Breaking`/`[!CAUTION]` in the body. Note
  the migration diff the PR gives. Unmarked PRs break things too: look for
  "renamed", "removed", "replaces", "is gone", "now requires", "`X` is now
  `Y`" and "was `X`" in every body. Confirm each one shipped in the last
  release (`git grep <old name> <release-sha> -- packages/`) before listing
  it; a rename of something added in this same release isn't breaking.
- **headline**: a dependency upgrade users must make (Effect, a framework
  major), a new provider or package, a new capability with a user-facing API,
  or a major bug fix (data loss, wrong resource deleted or taken over,
  deploys that hang or fail, large perf or bundle wins).
- **also**: smaller features and fixes users would notice.
- **skip**: internal only. CI, skills, lint and repo tooling, test-only PRs
  that fix no shipped behavior, distilled bumps without a user-visible change,
  docs restyles, and fix-ups of earlier PRs in the same release.

Group related PRs into one item: a stack of PRs for one feature is one
section, and a family of fixes (drift, ownership, local dev) is one bullet.

## 3. Plan before writing

Write the plan out first: the title, the breaking-change list, the ordered
headline sections with the PRs each one cites, and the also-list groups.

- **Title**: `2.0.0-beta.N - <three short items>`. It renders in the blog
  sidebar, so it must fit on one line.
- **Order the headlines** by how much they change a user's day: required
  upgrades (Effect) first, then new providers and packages, then the biggest
  new capabilities, then major fixes. There is no cap on the number of
  sections; a large release gets 25–30. Its size is set by what shipped.
- **A new user-facing API gets a snippet**, in its own section or in a
  section about its area (a "New AWS resources and options" section collects
  smaller ones). Never shrink one into a clause of an unrelated section: a
  reader skimming headings must find it. A PR that adds several APIs (a store
  that gains `accountId`, `workerName` and `domain` plus a new bootstrap
  command) is usually its own section.
- **Everything else** goes into `## Also in this release`, grouped by area
  (Cloudflare features, Cloudflare fixes, Local dev fixes, AWS features, AWS
  fixes, GCP, Domain, Auth, …), each group one bullet with its PR links.

## 4. Write it

File: `website/src/content/docs/blog/YYYY-MM-DD-beta-NN.md`, dated the
release day (ask if it isn't today). Frontmatter `title`, `date`,
`category: release` and a one-sentence `excerpt`.

- Open with two short paragraphs naming the headline features in bold.
- `:::caution` with **Breaking changes** at the top. Each item says what to
  do, with a `diff` snippet when code changes, and links its section below.
- One `##` per headline. One or two sentences, then a snippet of the
  user-facing API. Show DX, not implementation: what you write, what you get,
  the before/after error or output. Take snippets from the PR bodies, trim
  them, and check the names against the source (`grep` the export) since PRs
  get renamed in review.
- End a section with `Docs: [Page](/path)` links when a page covers it.
- Cite PRs inline as `([#NNN](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/pull/NNN))`.
- Credit external contributors by display name from `authors.txt`, linked to
  their GitHub profile: `Thanks [Name](https://github.com/login)!`. Use the
  login when there's no display name. PRs a maintainer opened on someone's
  behalf say so in the body ("carries #N by", "ported from", "supersedes");
  credit that person.
- End with `## Where to go next`: doc links, then
  `[CHANGELOG](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v200-betaNN)`
  and `[Compare v2.0.0-beta.N → v2.0.0-beta.N+1](https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/compare/v2.0.0-beta.N...v2.0.0-beta.N+1)`.

Format every snippet the way oxfmt would at an 80-column print width (the
blog's code column), and move trailing comments that overflow onto their own
line. oxfmt reads a top-level `yield*` as multiplication, so format such
snippets by hand or inside a temporary `function* () {}` wrapper.

Style: plain, direct sentences; no marketing adjectives; no "X just
happened" lists explaining a snippet. Every ```diff block needs a context line
at column 0 (a comment, an import, the outer call), and `+`/`-` lines are the
marker followed by the line's real indentation. Inline code that contains a
backtick uses double-backtick delimiters.

## 5. Check it

```sh
python3 -I .agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/check-post.py website/src/content/docs/blog/<post>.md /tmp/release-blog-<next>
```

It checks that every docs link and anchor resolves and that every diff block
passes the website build's odd-indent check. Fix every problem it reports.
It also lists every `feat`, `fix`, `perf` or `!` PR the post doesn't cite.
Each one must be a deliberate skip (a fix-up of another PR in this release,
test or CI only); cite the rest.

Then hand the post to the user with the headline plan (sections and the PRs
behind each), the breaking-change list, and anything you weren't sure about:
a PR whose user impact was unclear, a section you cut, or the date. Don't
commit, push or open a PR unless asked.

## 6. Tweets (when asked)

One tweet per major category, in the post's order: Effect, each headline
Domain feature, each headline provider feature, state, CLI, and one for the
bug fixes. Each tweet is one sentence plus a screenshot of its section.

**The sentence** states the user-facing change and, when the post has one,
its number: "a million accounts in 8 minutes", "plans are 270× faster".
Plain words, no hype, no hashtags, no emoji. Take every claim from the post,
not from memory.

**The screenshot** is the section's heading plus its code, diagram or table,
with the prose between them hidden. Run the docs dev server
(`cd website && bunx astro dev --ignore-lock`), list each heading's blocks,
then write a `shots.json` that picks them:

```sh
PW=$(ls -d node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@*/node_modules | tail -1)
URL=http://localhost:4321/blog/<post-slug>/
NODE_PATH=$PW bun .agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/screenshot-sections.mjs $URL --list
NODE_PATH=$PW bun .agents/skills/release-blog/scripts/screenshot-sections.mjs $URL /tmp/tweets-<next> shots.json
```

```json
{
  "01-effect-41": [["effect-41", "h"], ["effect-41", 1], ["effect-41", 3]],
  "02-domain-rollout": [
    ["deploys-roll-out-every-change-to-a-model", "h"],
    ["how-it-scales", 1],
    ["how-it-scales", 5]
  ]
}
```

Each entry is `[heading id, "h" | n]`, where `n` is the block index `--list`
prints under that heading; blocks can come from different headings. Images
are dark mode at 2× resolution, and animated figures render their last frame.
Pick the block that shows the change best: the diagram over the prose, the
failure output over the test code, the before/after table over the setup.
Open every image and check that no code line is cut off and no neighbouring
text shows.

Show each tweet inline with its image (`![](/tmp/tweets-<next>/NN-name.png)`),
save the text to `/tmp/tweets-<next>/tweets.md`, and note that no tweet has a
link yet. Never post them.

# Release overnight

This thread runs the whole release unattended, **one suite at a time**. It owns
every step: the clean slate, each run, the fixes, type-checking, the census
and the PRs. It launches no subagents or threads, and it runs nothing in
parallel with a live suite. Going slowly in series is the point. A live suite
under load produces fake failures, and parallel fixers on one account leak
into each other's census.

A provider is **done** when its whole suite passes in one run at the current
head and the census shows nothing new. The release is done when every
provider is done at the final head, `pnpm test:examples` passes, and the
account is clean. The user merges; you never do.

## 0. One question, then unattended

Ask once, up front, in a single question. Confirm three things: the scope
(default: everything in §2), that you'll nuke the testing account before each
step for the whole run, and any opt-in tags or paid add-ons to include
(default: none). **Nuking is destructive, so get an explicit yes.** After
that, never ask again. Take every decision yourself, record it in
`STATE.md`, and keep going. An answer you would have asked for goes in
the final report.

Don't end the turn until §6 is done. Ending the turn ends the night. Wait on
long runs with `t3_background_wait`, never with `sleep` or a polling loop.

## 1. Preflight and durable state

Start from the latest `origin/main`, on a fresh branch:

```sh
git status                      # must be clean; never git stash
git fetch origin main
git checkout -b release/overnight-$(date +%Y-%m-%d) origin/main
git log -1 --format='%H %s' origin/main   # record as "Base" in STATE.md
git submodule update --init -- submodules/distilled
```

Then run the rest of
[prepare-release §0](../prepare-release/SKILL.md#0-preflight): `pnpm install`,
pinned bun/node in `/tmp/release/env.sh`, `.env`, `aws sso login`, and
`pnpm exec tsrs -b`.

Don't merge `main` into the branch mid-run. A moving base would make every
`Passed at` meaningless. §6 picks up whatever landed overnight.

Keep the run's state in `/tmp/release/STATE.md` and update it after every
event. Context will be compacted many times overnight, and this file is how
you resume:

```md
# Release overnight 2026-10-31 — branch release/overnight-2026-10-31
Base: origin/main <sha> · Scope: all · opt-in: none · nuke authorized: yes
PRs: alchemy #— · distilled #— · floci #—

| # | Step | Command | Status | Passed at | Notes |
| - | ---- | ------- | ------ | --------- | ----- |
| 1 | Cloudflare | pnpm test:integration test/Cloudflare | done | a1b2c3d | |
| 2 | core unit | pnpm test | fixing (iter 2) | | Plan diff regression |

Gated: <test → typed tag + exact error>
Blocked (account, not code): <step → exact error>
```

**On every start, read `STATE.md` first.** If it exists, resume at the first
step that isn't `done`. Don't restart the night.

## 2. The steps, in order

Cloudflare goes first. State and most other suites deploy through
`packages/cloudflare`, so getting it green first keeps its failures out of
every later step. After that, cheap and narrow first, so a broken shared
layer shows up in minutes, not after AWS. Paths are relative to
`packages/integration-tests`:

| # | Step | Paths | `--concurrency` |
| - | ---- | ----- | --------------- |
| 1 | Cloudflare | `test/Cloudflare` | 16 |
| 2 | core unit | `pnpm test` (packages/alchemy) | default |
| 3 | core integration | `test/*.test.ts test/Bundle test/Cli test/Local test/Runtime test/Util test/Website` | 8 |
| 4 | building blocks | `test/Docker test/Redis test/Kubernetes test/SQL test/Drizzle test/Domain test/Auth test/DNS test/ACME` | 8 |
| 5 | Git, GitHub, Axiom, Stripe | one step each | 8 |
| 6 | Turso, Neon, Planetscale, Prisma | one step each | 8 |
| 7 | Hetzner, Railway, Fly | one step each | 8 |
| 8 | GCP | `test/GCP` | 16 |
| 9 | AWS | `test/AWS` | 32 |
| 10 | examples | `pnpm test:examples --profile testing` | — |

Every new top-level directory under `packages/integration-tests/test` gets a
step. If one is missing from this table, add it to steps 5–7 by size, and fix
this skill in the release PR. Never pass `--concurrency unbounded` or go
over 32. Never run a sequential monster file unfiltered in a fix iteration
(e.g. `Fly/BlueGreen.test.ts`). Its confirming run is the step's run.

## 3. One step

1. **Clean slate.** Run `pnpm nuke --yes --profile testing` and wait for it
   to finish. Then save `pnpm nuke --dry-run --profile testing` to
   `/tmp/release/census-<step>-before.txt`. What's left is residue
   (`scripts/nuke.sh` excludes). A holdout that survives two nukes is a stuck
   delete in that provider. Fix it in this step.
2. **Run** the step in the background, with the output written to a file:
   ```sh
   source /tmp/release/env.sh
   pnpm test:integration <paths> --profile testing --concurrency <n> \
     > /tmp/release/<step>-run-<k>.out 2>&1
   ```
   Wait on it with `t3_background_wait`. Start triage as soon as failures
   stream in (`grep -E "\] ✗ |failed to run|^Tests:"`). A test running far
   past its timeout is a hang. Read its log under `.alchemy/log/test/` and fix
   the cause.
3. **Census.** Once the run has finished, save `pnpm nuke --dry-run --profile
   testing` to `census-<step>-after.txt` and diff it against `-before`. Every
   new line is a leak, even from a green test. Leave leaks live while you fix
   them, since they're your evidence.
4. **Fix**, using the buckets and root-cause priority in
   [prepare-release §4](../prepare-release/SKILL.md#4-triage):
   provider bug > distilled patch > test fix. Never paper over a leak or an
   untyped error in a test. Re-run only the failing files, with `-t` when a
   file is long, until each one passes. A failure that also fails on `main`
   is still yours to fix.
5. **Budget.** Give a failure three fix iterations. If the blocker is
   platform behavior (entitlement, slow async provisioning, beta API), gate it
   on the typed tag with the exact error, keep an ungated probe, and move on.
   If the blocker is the account (billing, token permissions, a retired
   service), mark the step `blocked` with the exact error and move on. Never
   enable billing or edit shared tokens.
6. **Confirm.** Nuke, then run the **whole step once more** and take another
   census. The step is `done` only when that single run is green and the
   census diff is empty. Record the HEAD sha in `Passed at`.
7. **Gate and push.** Run `pnpm exec tsrs -b` and `pnpm docs:check-jsdoc` if
   any props changed. Commit one commit per fix, scoped (`fix(aws/ec2): …`),
   then push the alchemy branch and any distilled/floci branch (§5).

## 4. Keep earlier steps valid

A later fix can break an earlier step. The release needs every step to pass
at the **final** head, not just at the head where it once passed. After each
step, check what has changed since each `done` step passed:

```sh
git diff --name-only <passed-at>..HEAD
```

Mark a step `stale` when that list touches `packages/alchemy/`,
`packages/alchemy-test/`, its own provider packages, a package its tests
deploy through (most suites deploy through `packages/cloudflare` for state),
or the distilled/floci pins. Before step 10, re-run every stale step (§3.1–6)
in order until none is left. When a fix only touches one provider's own
package, the other steps stay valid.

## 5. PRs, linked

There are at most three PRs: alchemy, distilled and floci. Open the alchemy PR as a **draft** at
the first fix commit, and push after every step, so a crash at 4am loses
nothing. Use
[prepare-release §9](../prepare-release/SKILL.md#9-prs) for the standalone
distilled/floci clones, titles and bodies. On top of that:

- alchemy's branch pins `submodules/distilled` / `submodules/floci` at the
  current heads of their PR branches, and pushes a bump each time those
  branches move.
- Link them both ways. Put `Requires alchemy-run/distilled#X` (and floci) in
  the alchemy body, and `Required by alchemy-run/alchemy#Y` in each upstream
  body. Write the merge order distilled → floci → alchemy into the alchemy
  body.
- `link_pull_request` every PR to this thread.
- Mark the PRs ready (`gh pr ready`) only at §6, once everything is `done`.

## 6. Finish

After step 10 is done and no step is stale, `git fetch origin main`. If
`main` has moved past `Base`, merge it, resolve any conflicts, run
`pnpm exec tsrs -b`, and apply §4 to the merged changes. Re-run every step it
marks stale, and step 10 if any step re-ran. Repeat until a fetch finds
nothing new. The PR must be mergeable at a head that already contains the
latest `main`. Then nuke one last time and take a final census. It must show residue only. Then, and only then, end the
turn with the report:

```md
### Release ready at <sha> after one overnight pass. I recommend merging, in this order:

1. distilled — <what it types> — https://github.com/alchemy-run/distilled/pull/X
2. floci — <what it fixes> — https://github.com/alchemy-run/floci/pull/Z
3. alchemy — <K> fixes, <G> gated tests — https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/pull/Y

| Step | Tests | Result | Passed at |
| ---- | ----- | ------ | --------- |
| Cloudflare | 1577 | ✅ | a1b2c3d |
| AWS | 3361 | ✅ 3349 · 12 gated | f00ba47 |
| examples | 38 | ✅ | f00ba47 |

Gated: <test → typed tag + exact error>.
Blocked (account): <step → exact error>.
Decisions taken overnight: <ones you'd have asked about>.
Census: clean except <documented residue>.
```

After each upstream PR merges, the submodule has to be repointed at its
`main` merge commit and the steps that commit invalidates have to be re-run.
Say so in the report rather than claiming the release is final. Say plainly
what didn't run (out-of-scope steps, opt-in tags, blocked steps). Don't report
CI status in place of these results.

## Pitfalls

Everything in
[prepare-release's pitfalls](../prepare-release/SKILL.md#pitfalls-seen-in-practice)
applies here. In addition:

- **The SSO session expires overnight.** An AWS step failing in ~100ms at
  setup means the token is gone. Run `aws sso login` again. If that needs a
  human, mark the step `blocked` and go on to the non-AWS steps, then come
  back to it.
- **Never overlap nuke with a run**, and never start a step's run before its
  nuke has finished.
- **Steps share one account.** A leak from step 4 shows up in step 5's census
  unless step 4's confirming census was clean. Don't move on with a dirty
  census.

   If the blocker is the account (billing, token permissions, a retired
   service), mark the step `blocked` with the exact error and move on. Never
   enable billing or edit shared tokens.
6. **Confirm.** Nuke, then run the **whole step once more** and take another
   census. The step is `done` only when that single run is green and the
   census diff is empty. Record the HEAD sha in `Passed at`.
7. **Gate and push.** Run `pnpm exec tsrs -b` and `pnpm docs:check-jsdoc` if
   any props changed. Commit one commit per fix, scoped (`fix(aws/ec2): …`),
   then push the alchemy branch and any distilled/floci branch (§5).

## 4. Keep earlier steps valid

A later fix can break an earlier step. The release needs every step to pass
at the **final** head, not just at the head where it once passed. After each
step, check what has changed since each `done` step passed:

```sh
git diff --name-only <passed-at>..HEAD
```

Mark a step `stale` when that list touches `packages/alchemy/`,
`packages/alchemy-test/`, its own provider packages, a package its tests
deploy through (most suites deploy through `packages/cloudflare` for state),
or the distilled/floci pins. Before step 10, re-run every stale step (§3.1–6)
in order until none is left. When a fix only touches one provider's own
package, the other steps stay valid.

## 5. PRs, linked

There are at most three PRs: alchemy, distilled and floci. Open the alchemy PR as a **draft** at
the first fix commit, and push after every step, so a crash at 4am loses
nothing. Use
[prepare-release §9](../prepare-release/SKILL.md#9-prs) for the standalone
distilled/floci clones, titles and bodies. On top of that:

- alchemy's branch pins `submodules/distilled` / `submodules/floci` at the
  current heads of their PR branches, and pushes a bump each time those
  branches move.
- Link them both ways. Put `Requires alchemy-run/distilled#X` (and floci) in
  the alchemy body, and `Required by alchemy-run/alchemy#Y` in each upstream
  body. Write the merge order distilled → floci → alchemy into the alchemy
  body.
- `link_pull_request` every PR to this thread.
- Mark the PRs ready (`gh pr ready`) only at §6, once everything is `done`.

## 6. Finish

After step 10 is done and no step is stale, `git fetch origin main`. If
`main` has moved past `Base`, merge it, resolve any conflicts, run
`pnpm exec tsrs -b`, and apply §4 to the merged changes. Re-run every step it
marks stale, and step 10 if any step re-ran. Repeat until a fetch finds
nothing new. The PR must be mergeable at a head that already contains the
latest `main`. Then nuke one last time and take a final census. It must show residue only. Then, and only then, end the
turn with the report:

```md
### Release ready at <sha> after one overnight pass. I recommend merging, in this order:

1. distilled — <what it types> — https://github.com/alchemy-run/distilled/pull/X
2. floci — <what it fixes> — https://github.com/alchemy-run/floci/pull/Z
3. alchemy — <K> fixes, <G> gated tests — https://github.com/alchemy-run/alchemy/pull/Y

| Step | Tests | Result | Passed at |
| ---- | ----- | ------ | --------- |
| Cloudflare | 1577 | ✅ | a1b2c3d |
| AWS | 3361 | ✅ 3349 · 12 gated | f00ba47 |
| examples | 38 | ✅ | f00ba47 |

Gated: <test → typed tag + exact error>.
Blocked (account): <step → exact error>.
Decisions taken overnight: <ones you'd have asked about>.
Census: clean except <documented residue>.
```

After each upstream PR merges, the submodule has to be repointed at its
`main` merge commit and the steps that commit invalidates have to be re-run.
Say so in the report rather than claiming the release is final. Say plainly
what didn't run (out-of-scope steps, opt-in tags, blocked steps). Don't report
CI status in place of these results.

## Pitfalls

Everything in
[prepare-release's pitfalls](../prepare-release/SKILL.md#pitfalls-seen-in-practice)
applies here. In addition:

- **The SSO session expires overnight.** An AWS step failing in ~100ms at
  setup means the token is gone. Run `aws sso login` again. If that needs a
  human, mark the step `blocked` and go on to the non-AWS steps, then come
  back to it.
- **Never overlap nuke with a run**, and never start a step's run before its
  nuke has finished.
- **Steps share one account.** A leak from step 4 shows up in step 5's census
  unless step 4's confirming census was clean. Don't move on with a dirty
  census.

description: Build backends with @alchemy.run/domain (domain-driven design on Effect) - turn requirements into aggregates, commands, events, rejections, views, policies, sagas, projections, streams, external systems and Apis; lay them out in a monorepo (domain / server / web packages, kind-suffixed files); test them with stories; host them on Cloudflare Durable Objects with alchemy; and drive them from a foldkit frontend. ---

# Building with @alchemy.run/domain

`@alchemy.run/domain` models a backend as typed messages and pure state transitions. Commands are decided by aggregates, which record events. Views fold events into read models. Policies react to events. Sagas run long processes. Projections write outside the model. The same model runs in memory for tests and on Cloudflare Durable Objects in production.

Docs: https://alchemy.run/domain, with every page listed in https://alchemy.run/llms.txt. Every section here and in the reference files ends with a More link to the docs page that covers it in depth. A complete reference project: `examples/cloudflare-domain` in the alchemy repo (a bank with a foldkit app).

## Workflow

Work in this order. Each step has a reference file with templates.

1. **Break the requirements down** into building blocks. See [references/modeling.md](references/modeling.md).
2. **Lay out the monorepo**: a domain package, a server package, a web package, with one kind-suffixed file per block. See [references/layout.md](references/layout.md).
3. **Write each block** from its template. See [references/building-blocks.md](references/building-blocks.md).
4. **Specify behavior with stories** before and while you implement it. See [references/testing.md](references/testing.md).
5. **Host the model** on Cloudflare from the server package, export its traces, and deploy with one alchemy stack. See [references/hosting.md](references/hosting.md).
6. **Drive it from foldkit** in the web package. See [references/frontend.md](references/frontend.md).

More: [Tutorial, part 1](https://alchemy.run/domain/tutorial/part-1).

## From requirements to building blocks

Read the requirements as a story of facts, and name each kind of thing you find:

- A fact the business records, named in the past tense (`MoneyWithdrawn`): an **Event**.
- A request to change something, named `<Verb><Noun>` (`WithdrawMoney`): a **Command**.
- A way a request is refused (`InsufficientFunds`): a **Rejection**.
- A thing whose rules must hold in one transaction (one account's balance): an **Aggregate**. It decides commands against its state.
- A question someone asks (balance, statement, dashboard): a **View**, keyed by what it's about.
- "Whenever X happens, do Y": a **Policy**.
- A process with steps, waits and undo (move money: debit, credit, refund on failure): a **Saga**, started by a policy.
- Something outside the model you call (fraud scoring, payments): an **External System**.
- Writes to a store outside the model (a ledger table): a **Projection**. An ordered, readable log per key (account cards): a **Stream** that a projection appends to.
- Who can do and see what: an **Api** listing commands and reads, with **middleware** (sessions, MFA) and each block's `decide` or `validate` authorizing.

A rule that spans aggregates never becomes a cross-aggregate transaction. Give the invariant its own aggregate, keyed by what it protects (`UsernameClaim` keyed by username). Or reserve first and commit after, in a policy or saga, with a deadline for anything that waits.

More: [What is Domain-Driven Design?](https://alchemy.run/domain/what-is-ddd), [Domain Model](https://alchemy.run/domain/model).

## Conventions

- **One block per file, named `<Noun>.<kind>.ts`.** The kinds are `.aggregate`, `.command`, `.view`, `.policy`, `.saga`, `.projection`, `.stream`, `.external`, `.api` and `.model`. Plus `.middleware`, `.context` and `.rejection`. An aggregate's id lives in `<Aggregate>.id.ts` next to it. Plain values (`Money.ts`) and helpers keep plain names.
- **A command file holds the command, the events it records, and the rejections only it returns.** A rejection or event used by several commands gets its own file.
- **A block's implementation sits in its file** (`TransferExecutionLive` in `TransferExecution.policy.ts`), unless it touches infrastructure. Then it lives in the server package.
- **Folders are subdomains** (`Account/`, `Transfer/`). The model, Apis, middleware and request context sit at the package root.
- **The domain package imports only `@alchemy.run/domain` and `effect`.** Cloudflare, Stripe, databases and HTTP session handling belong to the server package.
- **One domain package per model (bounded context).** A second model is a second domain package; one server can host several.

More: [Project layout](https://alchemy.run/domain/project-layout).

## Rules that keep a model correct

- `decide` is pure, or an `Effect.fn` that reads only what its command's middleware provides (`yield* CurrentActor`). It returns events or a rejection; it never performs I/O.
- `evolve` only applies an event to state. It never decides anything. It and `reply` are total: they cover every state and never fail, because `decide` already refused what can't happen. Keep a state the event can't follow (`s._tag === "Open" ? { ...s, balance: e.balanceAfter } : s`), never a guard that throws.
- Events carry the outcome `decide` worked out (`balanceAfter`), so `evolve` copies it instead of repeating a rule.
- Every rejection a command can return is listed in its `rejects`. Callers handle each one with `Effect.catchTag`.
- Policies and projections run at least once. Make their effects idempotent: commands sent from a handler get deterministic ids, and stores key rows by `stream:seq`.
- Don't wait for a saga in a policy. `start` it, keyed by the aggregate it's about, and react to the events its steps record.
- A handler resolves its dependencies once in `toLayer` and requires nothing per call.
- Build one Layer and provide it once (`Layer.mergeAll`, `Layer.provide`). Never chain `Effect.provide`.
- Never `throw`. Fail with tagged errors (`Domain.Rejection`, `Schema.TaggedError`).
- Tracing is automatic. Record payload values only through a declaration's `attributes`, or with `Effect.annotateCurrentSpan` in an effectful handler. Make secrets `Schema.Redacted`, so they never reach a trace or a log.
- Test what the model does, through stories: events, replies, rejections, views and saga outcomes. Don't test a saga's internal steps.

More: [Domain Model: The aggregate decides, and everything commits at once](https://alchemy.run/domain/model#the-aggregate-decides-and-everything-commits-at-once), [Cloudflare: Count on these guarantees](https://alchemy.run/domain/cloudflare#count-on-these-guarantees).

## Checklist for a change

1. Name the new facts, commands and rejections. Put each command in its own `<Command>.command.ts` with its events and rejections.
2. Add the command to its aggregate's `commands`, with a `decide` branch for it and an `evolve` branch for each event.
3. Update the views, policies and projections that care about the new events.
4. Expose it through an Api, if a client sends or reads it, with the middleware it needs.
5. Write stories for the happy path, every rejection, and every policy reaction.
6. Run the domain package's tests, with one that expects `Domain.verify(Model)` to be empty. Then type-check the monorepo (`tsc -b`) and run the server and web tests.

  worktrees.

composition findings are reported, generated paths are named, and comparison
state follows the selected workflow's retention policy.

skills.name: changesets
skills.desc: Concise PR finalization changesets. Use when implementation scope is complete and focused validation has finished to classify release impact, consolidate the PR's existing changeset, or write its consumer release note.
skills.body:
---
name: changesets
description: Concise PR finalization changesets. Use when implementation scope is complete and focused validation has finished to classify release impact, consolidate the PR's existing changeset, or write its consumer release note.
---

Treat a changeset as the release note for the complete PR, not as a log of work
performed along the way. Finalize it after the current implementation scope and
focused validation are complete.

## Workflow

1. Inspect the complete diff from the merge base, including changeset files
   already introduced by the PR, and identify directly affected published
   packages.
2. Classify impact across source types, runtime behavior, entrypoints, required
   services, lifecycle, and persisted or wire data.
3. Perform the breaking audit below.
4. Record a reason no changeset is required, or update the PR's existing
   changeset. Create one only when the PR does not have one. When required, read
   [authoring.md](authoring.md).
5. Validate package names, frontmatter, bump policy, and a one-sentence
   consumer-facing description, longer only for breaks or required migration.

Do not include unrelated worktree changes.

## PR-level consolidation

The default is one changeset file per PR. One file can name several packages and
summarize several related fixes or additions. Successive prompts, commits, and
subtasks within the same PR update that file. If implementation resumes after a
changeset was drafted, revise it during the next finalization pass.

Use separate files only when a maintainer requests the split or the PR contains
independent changes that need separate release notes.

## Requirement

Create a changeset for observable runtime behavior changes, including bug
fixes; exported value or public type changes; entrypoint or export-map changes;
changes to required services, errors, ownership, defaults, or lifecycle; and
persisted, serialization, protocol, or wire-format changes.

Tests-only changes, behavior-preserving internal refactors, documentation or
JSDoc maintenance, and unpublished tooling normally do not need one. When
unclear, inspect exports and consumer-visible declarations rather than inferring
from source location.

## Breaking Audit

A change is breaking when valid existing consumer code, configuration, or data
must change to keep compiling or behaving according to the previous contract.
Audit every surface:

- **Names and locations:** exports, entrypoints, compatibility exports, and
  module paths.
- **Call compatibility:** parameters, accepted inputs, overload resolution,
  generic parameters, and defaults.
- **Result compatibility:** return and error types, output narrowing, members,
  inference, and required services.
- **Runtime contracts:** defaults, failures, interruption, concurrency,
  ordering, resource lifetime, acquisition, cleanup, and mutation.
- **Data compatibility:** persisted schemas, encodings, database layouts,
  protocols, and wire formats.

Additive exports, optional parameters, and behavior-preserving implementations
are normally non-breaking. A fix restoring the documented contract is normally
non-breaking but still needs a changeset when its operational impact is
consumer-visible. Verify representative existing calls when overload ordering,
structural assignability, or inference makes compatibility uncertain. API diff
output is mechanical evidence, not a semantic-version decision.

The task is complete when every affected contract and published package is
accounted for and either the no-changeset decision is explicit or the PR has one
consolidated, valid changeset by default. Its release note is one sentence of
consumer impact, plus migration steps for every break, with no implementation
detail.

Use the repository's AI documentation as targeted reference, not ambient
context:

1. Identify the Effect APIs and concepts involved in the change.
2. Search `LLMS.md` and `ai-docs/src` for those names and concepts, then read
   the matching sections and examples.
3. Apply the relevant guidance and inspect nearby source and tests for any
   repository-internal conventions not covered by the documentation.

The task is ready for implementation when every material Effect API or pattern
has matching local guidance, or the search has established that none exists.

## API conventions

Write option types inline in the signature by default. Mark fields `readonly`
and add `| undefined` to optional fields:

```ts
export const make = (options: {
  readonly capacity: number
  readonly strategy?: "dropping" | "sliding" | undefined
}): Effect.Effect<Queue> => ...
```

Declare a named options type only in these cases:

- A substantial set of options is shared across several APIs, so a named type
  keeps them in sync.
- The options type needs complex conditional logic, such as conditional or
  mapped types driven by type parameters.

A long option list for a single API is not on its own a reason to extract a
named type.

skills.body:
---
name: pull-requests
description: Pull request finalization. Use when a change works and is about to be opened as a pull request, or when updating or continuing an existing one.
---

A pull request is ready when its tests, implementation, comments, and changeset
are each the simplest that cover the intended behavior. Draft PRs can be used
earlier; finishing means making the PR ready for review.

## Workflow

Run each step in a fresh-context subagent when available; otherwise run it
yourself. Pass along the task context and prior results so each step can check its gate.

1. Keep tests focused. Read [test-development](../test-development/SKILL.md) for
   test placement and type. Cover each intended behavior once, in the existing
   test file for the module.
   For changes needing no tests, record why.
   Continue when removing any remaining case would leave intended behavior
   uncovered, or no tests are needed.
2. Simplify the implementation. With the tests passing, look for a simpler or
   more idiomatic version: reuse helpers and patterns from nearby source and
   [effect-development](../effect-development/SKILL.md), and remove debugging
   code, scaffolding, and changes unrelated to the task.
   Continue when applicable targeted tests pass and every hunk in the diff
   from the merge base is required by the task.
3. Review the full diff from the merge base as a maintainer would: correctness,
   failure and interruption paths, resource cleanup, naming and API
   consistency with neighboring modules, and documentation. Fix findings and
   review again.
   Continue when a review pass produces no findings.
4. Clean up. Remove comments that restate code or narrate the change; keep the
   rest short and about why. Finalize the changeset with
   [changesets](../changesets/SKILL.md).
   Continue when comments explain only what code cannot, and the changeset
   describes the final consumer impact or the no-changeset reason is recorded.
5. Run the validation in the [AGENTS.md validation table](../../AGENTS.md#validation)
   for each change type in the diff. Fix failures caused by the change; if
   fixes alter the diff, repeat the affected passes.
   Continue when applicable checks pass or commands that cannot run and their
   blockers are recorded.
6. Open or update the pull request. Title: a short imperative summary.
   Description: the problem addressed, notable decisions, and `Closes #<issue>` for each
   GitHub issue resolved. Do not narrate the diff. Mark the PR ready for review.
   Continue when the final changes are pushed, the description matches the
   final diff, and the PR is ready for review.

The task is complete when each step's gate holds, validation has passed or
been reported as not runnable with reasons, and the pull request is ready for
review with a description matching the final diff.

description: Vendored assets. Use when importing or updating checked-in third-party or externally generated JavaScript, CSS, registries, schemas, snapshots, or Scalar, Swagger, and MIME artifacts.
---

Treat upstream artifacts as supply-chain inputs. Change their generator or
documented import source, then regenerate; generated output is review evidence,
not an editing surface.

## Workflow

1. **Trace ownership.** Identify the artifact, generator or exact import
   procedure, upstream source/version, license, consumers, tests, and shipped
   package or bundle. Search by asset and upstream project name to find current
   packaging scripts, generated artifacts, consumers, and history.
   Continue when every input and consumer is accounted for.
2. **Pin provenance.** Resolve moving URLs, tags, branches, and omitted versions
   to an immutable release or artifact. Record project, version, path or URL,
   and digest in the generator or maintenance header. Omit a digest only when
   another enforced immutable source is recorded.
   Continue when a future run cannot silently select different bytes.
3. **Clear the license gate.** Verify release metadata, license files, bundled
   notices, and the license trail retained in the distributed form.
   Continue when every distributed artifact has a verified retained license trail.
4. **Regenerate.** Improve the generator or import reference first. Recover an
   exact procedure for generatorless assets; add a deterministic script only
   for recurring updates. Record a one-off procedure beside the artifact. A
   clean rerun must produce no diff.
5. **Audit the complete diff.** Account for behavior, URLs and runtime fetches,
   source maps, notices, encoding, format changes, and additions or removals.
   For browser assets, also read [browser-assets.md](browser-assets.md).
   Continue when every change is attributable and suspicious content is resolved
   or reported.
6. **Clear test and size gates.** Record byte sizes before and after, use
   focused consumer tests, and compare bundle size or composition when shipped
   JavaScript, CSS, or registry output changes materially. Compare that output
   against the pre-update revision rather than measuring only current size.
   Continue when focused checks pass and every non-trivial size delta is explained.
7. **Close release impact.** Apply root changeset routing for consumer-visible
   behavior, browser support, wire data, or meaningful shipped-size changes.
   Generated sections owned by barrels, AI docs, or migration tooling remain
   with the owners named in root instructions.

The task is complete when every input and consumer is accounted for, provenance
and licenses are immutable and retained, regeneration is deterministic, every
output change and non-trivial size delta is explained, focused checks pass or
are reported as not runnable, and release impact is recorded.
